Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We will show that the minimum is \(499\).

First, from \(i=j\) we get

\[
|A_i|=i.
\]

If \(g=\gcd(i,j)\), then \(A_g\subseteq A_i\cap A_j\), and

\[
|A_g|=g=|A_i\cap A_j|,
\]

so in fact

\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_g.
\]

In particular, if \(d\mid n\), then \(A_d\subseteq A_n\).

Now restrict to the divisors of \(250\). Let \(D\) be the set of positive divisors of \(250\):

\[
D=\{1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250\}.
\]

For \(x\in A_{250}\), define

\[
T_x=\{d\in D:x\in A_d\}.
\]

This finite set is upward closed under divisibility and closed under gcd, so if \(m=\gcd T_x\), then \(m\in T_x\) and

\[
T_x=\{d\in D:m\mid d\}.
\]

Call \(m\) the label of \(x\). For each \(m\in D\), let \(c_m\) be the number of elements of \(A_{250}\) with label \(m\). For every \(d\in D\),

\[
|A_d|=\sum_{m\mid d} c_m=d.
\]

By Möbius inversion, \(c_m=\varphi(m)\). Thus

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|l}
m & c_m & \{d\in D\setminus\{250\}:m\mid d\}\\\hline
250 & 100 & \varnothing\\
125 & 100 & \{125\}\\
25 & 20 & \{25\}\\
50 & 20 & \{50\}\\
10 & 4 & \{10,50\}\\
5 & 4 & \{5,10,25,50,125\}\\
2 & 1 & \{2,10,50\}\\
1 & 1 & \{1,2,5,10,25,50,125\}
\end{array}
\]

The sum of these counts is \(250\), as expected.

For the sum of maxima, it suffices to assume the \(250\) elements of \(A_{250}\) are exactly \(1,2,\dots,250\). We order the classes of labels from largest to smallest assigned numbers. A standard adjacent-swap argument shows that in an optimal arrangement each class occupies a contiguous block.

If the block order is \(\pi\), and \(U_i\) is the union of the divisor-sets from the table for the first \(i\) blocks, then the sum of maxima is

\[
\sum_{i=1}^8 c_{\pi_i}\bigl(1+|U_i|\bigr).
\]

Using the exchange condition implied by the table, an optimal block order is

\[
250,\ 125,\ 25,\ 50,\ 10,\ 5,\ 2,\ 1
\]

(up to swapping \(25\) and \(50\)). In this order the union sizes are \(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\). Hence the minimum possible sum is

\[
100\cdot1+100\cdot2+20\cdot3+20\cdot4+4\cdot5+4\cdot6+1\cdot7+1\cdot8.
\]

Thus

\[
100+200+60+80+20+24+7+8=499.
\]

This value is attainable: assign labels as follows and set \(A_n\) to be the set of all assigned numbers whose label divides \(n\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
250&:\;151,\dots,250,\\
125&:\;51,\dots,150,\\
25&:\;31,\dots,50,\\
50&:\;11,\dots,30,\\
10&:\;7,\dots,10,\\
5&:\;3,4,5,6,\\
2&:\;2,\\
1&:\;1.
\end{aligned}
\]

For other labels, use unused positive integers. Then \(|A_n|=\sum_{d\mid n}\varphi(d)=n\), and intersections give gcds. The maxima for \(d\mid250\) are

\[
1,2,6,10,50,30,150,250,
\]

which sum to \(499\).

Therefore the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}.
\]
